1.
Proceedings in the present case initiated by filing of DAR in MACT No.297/2019 Page 1 FIR No.168/2019 of PS Harsh Vihar u/s 279/304A IPC.

As per the facts on 18.04.2019 one tractor trolley bearing registration no.UP 14DU 5025 being driven by respondent no.1 herein Abhay Singh @ Chauhan, in trolley there were bricks kept and driver of the tractor was driving the same in a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
Deceased Bharat Singh was sitting by the side of driver.
When driver of the tractor suddenly took the brake, due to impact the deceased sitting by the side of driver fell down and the tyre of the tractor crushed the deceased.
After the accident deceased was taken to GTB Hospital where he was found to be unconscious and unresponsive.
Initially MLC was prepared however on the same day deceased died.

Intimation was sent to MACT Cell regarding Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
1 death in road side accident.
After registration of the FIR, during investigation eye witnesses Ramu @ Rahul, Asif seen the incident and gave the statement to the IO.
Offending vehicle i.e. tractor trolley bearing registration no. UP 14DU 5025 owned by respondent no.2 Mahipal Singh.
Upon serving notice u/s 133 M.V. Act, certificate of registration, insurance documents were furnished.
Offending vehicle was found to be insured with Magma HDI General Insurance Company (respondent no.3).
During the investigation post mortem of the deceased was got conducted.
2. Upon filing the DAR, respondents i.e. driver, owner as well as counsel for the insurance company of offending vehicle appeared, they were provided the copy of DAR.
All the legal heirs of deceased i.e. parents were brought on record.
3. Reply to the DAR was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 wherein it is pleaded that no accident has occurred by rash and negligent driving of the vehicle by respondent no.1.
It is pleaded that vehicle was otherwise insured.
MACT No.297/2019 Page 2 4.
Insurance company also filed the reply to the DAR taking the objection that DAR has been got filed by respondent no.1 and 2 in collusion with police for taking unjust compensation.

It is stated that vehicle no. UP 14DU 5025, though was insured with the insurance company vide policy no.P0019400002/4107/111249 from 15.09.2018 to 14.09.2018 in category of "commercial vehicle class D".

It is pleaded that since deceased was travelling in the insured tractor at the time of alleged accident, which was violation of section 149(2) of M.V. Act as there was breach of permit in respect of vehicle in question.
Policy for vehicle in question was issued for goods carriage, as such it could not include any passenger in the vehicle.
Carrying passengers in goods vehicle is contrary to mandate of statute.

In case the Tribunal comes to conclusion of awarding of compensation regarding death of deceased who was traveling in insured vehicle as gratuitous passenger, his risk was not covered under the policy.
As such insurance company is not liable for the amount of compensation if any payable.

5. On the basis of pleadings of parties, ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal framed following issues on 27.02.2020 :
(1)Whether Respondent No.1 was driving the offending vehicle No. UP-14-DU-5025 on 18.04.2019 at about 9.57 PM at Mandoli Chowk, Near Chaman Market Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Harsh Vihar, in rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh.Bharat Singh?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
6. In order to substantiate its case petitioner examined two witnesses i.e. PW1 herself Sharda and eye witness PW2 Asif.
Respondent MACT No.297/2019 Page 3 no.3/insurance company examined one witness R3W1.

Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
2 7.
I have heard Sh.R.K. Pathak, ld. Counsel for petitioner as well as Sh.Ved Tripathi, ld. Counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have gone through the submissions.
Issue No.1 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

sentences.text: In the facts of the present case petitioner (PW1) in her deposition has specifically testified that her son late Bharat Singh was only bread earner of family and left behind two persons i.e. PW1 being mother and father Ram Bahadur Singh.
PW1 deposed that her son ws aged about 24 years and was working as labour in Delhi and earning about Rs.15,000/- per month.
She deposed that her son along with other labour Ramu, Rahul was working on 18.04.2019 with tractor trolley no.UP 14DU 5025 for loading and unloading of bricks.
The vehicle was being driven by its drive and labour were sitting in trolley.
When said tractor trolley reached near MACT No.297/2019 Page 4 Mandoli Chowk, near Chaman Market, Delhi, it was being driven with very high speed in a rash and negligent manner.
Due to head collusion the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body as he was stuck in the vehicle.
PW1 deposed that due to sudden impact of hit by offending vehicle driven by Abhay Singh, son of PW1 sustained grievous injuries.
Deceased was rescued by the passerby and was taken to GTB Hospital where he was declared dead.
PW1 deposed that due to death of her son, she and her family loss their future as they have no source of income because family was dependent on deceased.
PW1 proved her Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/1, Aadhar card of her husband Rama Bahadur Singh as Ex.PW1/2 and copy of DAR along with final report as Ex.PW1/3.
10 . PW1 was duly cross examined on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner as well as on behalf of respondent no.3/insurance company.
In cross-examination PW1 stated that her elder son Bharat has expired who was doing work of labour.
She admitted that she has not filed any income proof of her son.
She also admitted that she has not filed any identify proof of deceased.
She admitted that she is not an eye witness to the accident and she has not filed any residence proof of Delhi.
11. PW2 Asif deposed that on 18.04.2019 between 9.30 to 10.00 p.m., he was sitting in his shop (sugarcane juice shop) situated at main Mandoli Chowk, Chaman Market, Mandoli Village, Delhi.
He saw one tractor bearing no. UP 14DU 5025 was coming from back school road and going to bank colony.
The tractor reached at Mandoli at very high speed and driver of tractor took brake suddenly.

PW2 deposed that one person who was sitting on the tractor besides the driver fell down and came Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
3 under the back wheel of tractor and crossed the said person by which that person MACT No.297/2019 Page 5 sustained fatal injuries.
PW2 rushed to the place of accident and saw that he was unconscious.
Some person called 100 number and ambulance took the injured for hospitalization and then PW2 came back to his shop.

12. During cross-examination on behalf of R3/insurance company PW2 stated that distance between accident place and his shop was near about 8 to 10 steps and at the time of accident there was heavy traffic on the road.
There was no divider in between of the road.
PW2 stated that at the time of accident there was dark due to non functioning of street light situated at Mandoli Chowk.
He stated that 3 to 4 persons were sitting on the tractor which was passed in front of him.
PW2 specifically stated that he observed tractor no.UP 14DU 5025 by going near to that tractor at the place of accident.
He voluntarily stated that there was sufficient light on the road and place of accident with the help of light of shops situated at the road side.

He stated that he used to run his shop from 7 a.m.
to 11 p.m. daily.
He denied that deceased fell from trolley of the tractor.
During cross-examination on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2, PW2 stated that direction of the tractor was correct side.
He denied that driver of the offending vehicle was driving his vehicle by following rules and regulations of traffic.
He also denied that he was not present at the time of accident on the spot.
He stated that he did not recognize driver of tractor because he flew away from the spot after the accident.
PW2 denied that death of deceased occurred due to his own negligence and not because of negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
13. From the testimony of eye witness PW2, it is is well established that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending tractor no.UP 14DU 5025 being driven by respondent no.1.
PW2 has specifically stated that on the day of accident he saw the offending MACT No.297/2019 Page 6 tractor coming from back school road and going to bank colony.

He also stated that tractor reached Mandoli at very high speed and driver of the tractor took sudden brakes due to which person sitting on the tractor beside driver fell down and came under the rear wheel of the tractor and wheel of tractor crossed the said person due to which he sustained fatal injuries.
Though this witness was cross-examined, however respondents failed to put any dent to his testimony.

Thus from the testimony of PW2, it is well established that offending tractor was being driven in very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner on the day of incident and deceased came under the wheels of tractor due to which he sustained fatal injuries.
14. Testimony of PW2 has duly been corroborated by DAR and accompanying documents Ex.PW1/3.
Copy of FIR no.168/2019 of PS Harsh Vihar shows registration of criminal case in respect of accident in question for offence u/s 279/304A IPC.
Respondent no.1 being driver of the offending tractor no.UP 14DU 5025 was arrested in said FIR on the day of accident i.e. 19.04.2019 itself.
Notice u/s 133 M.V. Act issued to the owner of offending tractor shows that owner informed to police that on the day of accident said tractor was being driven by respondent no.1 Abhay Singh.
Mechanical inspection report of tractor no. UP 14DU 5025 further shows that the said tractor was it was in working condition and its braking system was duly working.
Testimony of PW2 has also been corroborated by site plan of the place of accident.

Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
4 15.

Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reference may be given to judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v. Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated MACT No.297/2019 Page 7 24.01.2020, wherein it has been observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

sentences.text:
On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.
955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle,
(ii) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR,
wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Hence,
this contention of the counsel of the appellant also falls face down.

There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of driver."
16.

Besides above, MLC of deceased shows that he was the case of RTA (road traffic accident) and it was brought to GTB Hospital in MACT No.297/2019 Page 8 unresponsive state and he was declared brought death in casualty.
Postmortem report of deceased further shows that he received injuries on head, face, right shoulder, chest, abdomen, left forearm and wrist joint.
Examination of chest of deceased as per PM report shows that there were fractures of all his ribs, multiple deep laceration on each lobe and multiple cavity deep lacerations on left ventricle.
Cause of death of deceased was hemorrhagic shock as a result of ante mortem injury to chest and abdomen produced by blunt force impact.

17. In view of the above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Bharat Singh.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.

Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
5 Issue No.2 18.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, both petitioner i.e. parents of deceased are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

19. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 20.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Bharat MACT No.297/2019 Page 9 Singh.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
6 19.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) MACT No.297/2019 Page 10 The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
21.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
MACT No.297/2019 Page 11  PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Medical Expenses:
22.
In the present case it is admitted case of the parties that deceased was straightaway taken to GTB Hospital after he was crushed under the wheels of offending vehicle in question.
As per MLC of deceased he was declared brought dead in the hospital itself.
Since deceased was not given any treatment what to say expenditure on his medical treatment, therefore no question arises for computing any medical expenses in respect of injuries sustained by him.

Age of deceased :
Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
7 23.
The petitioner (PW1) in her affidavit has deposed that her deceased son was aged 24 years on the day of accident.
Though PW1 was cross-examined on behalf of respondents, however age of deceased has not been disputed by any of the respondents.
The DAR filed filed by police also shows that deceased was aged 24 years at the relevant time.
Death report annexed with DAR Ex.PW1/3 also shows that deceased was aged 24 years.
Even no evidence in rebuttal has been brought by any of the respondents disputing age of deceased.
Accordingly, the age of deceased on the date of accident (18.04.2019) was 24 years.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
24.
Petitioner (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased son was having good physique and was working as labour and was earning at about Rs.15,000/- per month.
This fact has been disputed by the respondents.

25. Ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company has submitted that no evidence has been led by petitioner in support of her claim that deceased used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month while working as MACT No.297/2019 Page 12 labour at the time of accident.
He also submitted that even petitioner has not brought any evidence on record to show that deceased was resident of Delhi.

He submits that if this Tribunal comes to conclusion that petitioners are entitled for compensation on account of death of deceased due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, in the absence of any proof of earning by the petitioners and the fact that there is no evidence showing that deceased was resident of Delhi, petitioners can only be awarded compensation while treating income of deceased as minimum wages of unskilled worker in State of U.P.
26.
I find force in the contention of ld. counsel for R3/insurance company that there is no evidence on record to prove that deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month at the time of accident.
The onus to prove the income of the deceased was on the petitioners.
However no evidence was brought on record by petitioners to substantiate this fact.

PW1 has filed on record copy of her Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/1 and copy of Aadhar Card of her husband as Ex.PW1/2 which show that they are residents of Panchsheel Bhopura, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

Thus, in the absence of any evidence regarding income of deceased and he being resident of Delhi,
this Tribunal comes to conclusion that deceased was resident of Uttar Pradesh on the day of accident and monthly income of deceased is computed equivalent to minimum wages paid to unskilled worker of Uttar Pradesh in April 2019 which comes to be Rs.8,012.73 per month.

Application of Multiplier:
27.
As held above, deceased was 24 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 MACT No.297/2019 Page 13 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

sentences.text:
In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
8

the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:
 MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5
Age group between 66 and above 28.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against 24 years of age of the deceased to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
29.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
MACT No.297/2019 Page 14 (iv)

In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
30. The deceased can be considered a temporary employee.
In view of the above said judgment, an addition of 40% of the income of deceased (aged 24 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
31.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid Dar - Sharda vs Abhay Singh on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967809/
9 down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six) MACT No.297/2019 Page 15 32.

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by two petitioners i.e. parents of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by two dependents, one-third of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
33.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

34. Considering the aforementioned factors, the total compensation is calculated as under:

Monthly income of deceased (A) Rs.8,012.73  2. Add future prospect (B) @ 40% Rs.3,205/-
3.

expenses of the deceased (C) MACT No.297/2019 Page 16 4.

Annual loss of dependency (Dx12) Rs.89,744.76 7.
Total loss of dependency (Dx12xE=F) Rs.16,15,405.68 8.

Medical expenses (G) Nil.
9. Compensation for loss of consortium (I) Rs.96,000/-
(48,000 X 2)

11.

35.
Thus, petitioners in this case shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.17,47,406/- only.
INTEREST ON AWARD 36.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 37.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
38. It is argued by ld. Counsel for the petitioner that vehicle in question was duly insured and therefore respondent no.3/insurance company is liable to pay the amount of compensation.

On the other hand counsel for respondent no.3 submitted that the tractor-trolley in question was being used as a goods carriage, though it was insured with respondent no.3 but such insurance was under the category of "commercial vehicle class D".

Ld. Counsel for insurance company submits that deceased was traveling as an unauthorized passenger in a goods vehicle, as such the risk MACT No.297/2019 Page 17 regarding death caused to him due to use of the tractor-trolley was not covered under the insurance policy.

While referring to the terms of the policy and policy note, ld. Counsel submits that even from the policy note it would be evident that said tractor had sitting capacity of one as per registration certificate.
As such any person apart from driver, traveling in goods carriage was contrary to the terms of the policy and statute.

Counsel for respondent no.3 relied upon judgments of Apex Court in New India Assurance Company vs. Asha Rani (2001) 6 SCC 724,
Oriental Insurance Company vs. Devi Reddy vs. Konda Reddy and Ors.

sentences.text: Having taken into consideration the submissions.
Admittedly in the present case tractor-trolley was being used for transporting bricks and therefore would be considered to be a goods carriage.
